summary: Full-extraction pass cbi-usa4 over 20 US EB-5 documents. USCIS quarterly all-forms reports FY2020-FY2026Q3: every EB-5 form row and cell (quarter and fiscal-year received, approved, denied, completions, pending, median processing time) for I-526 (all editions), I-829, I-924/I-924A and I-956/I-956F/G/H/K; USCIS I-526/I-526E receipts by month, set-aside and country of birth FY2022-FY2025 (every cell, all totals check); approved EB-5 petitions awaiting visas by country (2024-2026); GAO-15-696 and GAO-16-828 programme figures; SEC case figures (Chicago Convention Center, Jay Peak); statutory visa numbers, set-aside shares and processing goals from the 1990, 1992 and 2022 Acts.

observations.location: PDF p. 43 (printed p. 38)
observations.quote: the EB-5 Program has created a minimum of 73,730 jobs and more than $11.2 billion in investments
observations.notes: USCIS figure relayed by GAO: jobs "created" estimated by multiplying the number of investors with an approved Form I-829 by 10 (the minimum job requirement), not counted jobs. GAO found the method not valid or reliable (may over- or understate). "A minimum of"; same sentence as the existing USD 11.2 billion row.

observations.location: PDF p. 21 (printed p. 16)
observations.quote: the total number of EB-5 visas issued increased from almost 3,000 in fiscal year 2011 to over 9,000 in fiscal year 2014, according to State data
observations.notes: Rounded ("almost 3,000"), State Department data relayed by GAO; the report does not say whether adjustments of status inside the US are included.

observations.location: PDF p. 21 (printed p. 16)
observations.quote: the total number of EB-5 visas issued increased from almost 3,000 in fiscal year 2011 to over 9,000 in fiscal year 2014, according to State data
observations.notes: Rounded lower bound ("over 9,000"), State Department data relayed by GAO; the report does not say whether adjustments of status are included.

observations.location: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 4)
observations.quote: In fiscal year 2014, the maximum number of visas available were allocated for the EB-5 Program—approximately 10,000 annually, with about 95 percent of the investments in regional center projects.
observations.notes: Share of EB-5 investments made in regional center projects ("about"). The same sentence says the maximum of about 10,000 visas was allocated in FY2014 (not recorded separately: statutory ceiling).

observations.location: PDF p. 24 (printed p. 19)
observations.quote: From January 2013 through January 2015, SEC officials reported receiving over 100 tips, complaints, and referrals related to possible securities fraud violations and the EB-5 Program.
observations.notes: Lower bound ("over 100"). SEC officials cited by GAO; "just over half" led to further SEC investigation or referral to other law enforcement (share not recorded).

observations.location: PDF p. 25 (printed p. 20)
observations.quote: as of May 2015, over half (35) of the 59 open investigations tracked by the program primarily involved securities fraud issues.
observations.notes: Open investigations tracked by USCIS FDNS that primarily involved securities fraud; part of the 59 already recorded (no category).

observations.location: PDF p. 29 (printed p. 24), footnote 45; also PDF pp. 28-29 (printed pp. 23-24)
observations.quote: FDNS currently has 21 authorized positions; the office had 12 employees onboard as of May 2015.
observations.notes: Authorized positions in USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security (FDNS) for EB-5; the text says hiring 8 more "will bring the total authorized FDNS EB-5 staff from 13 to 21".

observations.location: PDF p. 29 (printed p. 24), footnote 45
observations.quote: FDNS currently has 21 authorized positions; the office had 12 employees onboard as of May 2015.
observations.notes: FDNS EB-5 staff actually on board (headcount).

observations.location: PDF p. 40 (printed p. 35)
observations.quote: in 2014, USCIS began increasing its staffing from 9 adjudicators to 58 adjudicator officers and 22 economists as of June 2015
observations.notes: Immigrant Investor Program Office adjudicator officers (headcount).

observations.location: PDF p. 40 (printed p. 35)
observations.quote: in 2014, USCIS began increasing its staffing from 9 adjudicators to 58 adjudicator officers and 22 economists as of June 2015
observations.notes: Immigrant Investor Program Office economists (headcount).

observations.location: PDF p. 40 (printed p. 35)
observations.quote: in 2014, USCIS began increasing its staffing from 9 adjudicators to 58 adjudicator officers and 22 economists as of June 2015
observations.notes: Adjudicators before the increase that began in 2014 (exact date not given; period set to the year the increase began).

observations.location: PDF pp. 40-41 (printed pp. 35-36)
observations.quote: IPO program managers estimated that as of fiscal year 2015, about 95 percent of EB-5 Program petitioners used economic models to estimate job creation, with about 90 percent of those petitioners using RIMS II.
observations.notes: Estimate by Immigrant Investor Program Office managers, relayed by GAO.

observations.location: PDF pp. 40-41 (printed pp. 35-36)
observations.quote: about 95 percent of EB-5 Program petitioners used economic models to estimate job creation, with about 90 percent of those petitioners using RIMS II.
observations.notes: Share of the petitioners who used economic models (not of all petitioners) that used the RIMS II model; footnote 66: the other 10 percent used IMPLAN, REDYN or REMI.

observations.location: PDF pp. 42-43 (printed pp. 37-38)
observations.quote: IPO program managers stated that approximately 90 percent of immigrant investors qualify for a reduced investment amount—$500,000 instead of $1 million
observations.notes: Share of investors qualifying for the reduced (targeted employment area) amount, as stated by IPO managers in 2015; no period given (dataset convention: year of the statement, basis unspecified).

observations.location: PDF p. 43 (printed p. 38)
observations.quote: The remaining 10 percent of immigrant investors pay twice that amount to participate in projects that are not limited to these locations.
observations.notes: Share investing the full USD 1 million outside targeted employment areas, per IPO managers (2015); no period given.

observations.location: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 39)
observations.quote: according to DHS's 2013 Yearbook of Immigration Statistics, about 32 immigrant investors paid $1 million instead of $500,000 into the EB-5 Program in fiscal year 2013
observations.notes: Investors who invested the full USD 1 million rather than the reduced USD 500,000 ("about"), DHS Yearbook data relayed by GAO. GAO adds that this is "a total difference of $16 million not counted by USCIS" (a GAO calculation, not recorded).

observations.location: PDF p. 45 (printed p. 40), footnote 77
observations.quote: the number of immigrant investors who filed an approved Form I-526 to participate in the program from program inception through fiscal year 2011 (approximately 10,000)
observations.notes: Investors with approved Form I-526 petitions from programme inception (GAO elsewhere: fiscal year 1990) through FY2011, approximate; GAO analysis of USCIS data.

observations.location: PDF p. 45 (printed p. 40), footnote 77
observations.quote: the number of immigrant investors who filed an approved Form I-829 through fiscal year 2014 to report successful completion of the program requirements (approximately 7,400)
observations.notes: Investors with approved Form I-829 petitions through FY2014 (from inception), approximate; GAO analysis of USCIS data. The remaining approximately 2,600 of the FY1990-FY2011 I-526 cohort did not file, were denied, or were pending.

observations.location: PDF pp. 44-45 (printed pp. 39-40)
observations.quote: approximately 26 percent of all EB-5 Program immigrant investors who entered the program from its inception year through fiscal year 2011 may not have completed the process to show funds spent and jobs created with an approved I-829 as of the fiscal year ending in 2014.
observations.notes: Cohort: investors with approved I-526 petitions from inception through FY2011 (about 10,000); share without an approved I-829 by end FY2014 (did not file, denied or pending). GAO analysis.

observations.location: PDF p. 47 (printed p. 42)
observations.quote: In one case, about 450 immigrant investors contributed 30 percent (approximately $225 million) of the capital toward a nearly $750 million total investment in a regional center project
observations.notes: One unnamed regional center project whose IPO file GAO reviewed (count for a single project, not an average). All 450 investors obtained permanent residence by claiming all of about 10,500 jobs; GAO estimates only 315 would have qualified on a pro rata basis (counterfactual, not recorded).

observations.location: PDF p. 47 (printed p. 42)
observations.quote: about 450 immigrant investors contributed 30 percent (approximately $225 million) of the capital toward a nearly $750 million total investment in a regional center project
observations.notes: EB-5 capital in one unnamed regional center project (approximate); total project investment "nearly $750 million".

observations.location: PDF p. 47 (printed p. 42)
observations.quote: about 450 immigrant investors contributed 30 percent (approximately $225 million) of the capital toward a nearly $750 million total investment in a regional center project
observations.notes: Single project (not a mean or median over projects).

observations.location: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 39)
observations.quote: we reviewed one project with about 450 immigrant investors that created over 10,500 jobs, or about 23 jobs per immigrant investor
observations.notes: Jobs credited to one regional center project by economic modelling of total project spending (footnote 85), "over 10,500"; USCIS counted only the 10-job minimum (4,500). About 23 jobs per investor (GAO division, not recorded).

observations.location: PDF p. 18 (printed p. 14)
observations.quote: FDNS has increased its number of authorized positions from 21 to 25 full-time equivalent staff and has added student intern positions and administrative support.
observations.notes: Authorized FDNS EB-5 positions; the report reflects status around August 2016 (audit Nov 2015-Sept 2016; exact date not given). Previously 21 (also in GAO-15-696).

observations.location: PDF p. 16 (printed p. 12)
observations.quote: a total of 50 site visits in four different states are planned. An agency official stated that the first site visits began in August 2016.
observations.notes: Planned FDNS random, unannounced site-visit pilot (a plan, not visits conducted); first visits began August 2016.

observations.location: PDF p. 19 (printed p. 15)
observations.quote: the program anticipates receiving around 14,000 petitions and applications a year, and the average submission is approximately 1,000 pages in length, for a cumulative total of about 14 million pages
observations.notes: All EB-5 petitions and applications expected per year according to USCIS documentation cited by GAO ("around"). The page counts (about 1,000 per filing, 14 million a year) are not recorded.

observations.location: PDF p. 19 (printed p. 15)
observations.quote: the average review time for an EB-5 filing can range from 5.5 hours for an I-829 removal of conditions petition to 40 hours for an I-924 application for a new regional center.
observations.notes: Average review time per filing according to USCIS documentation cited by GAO; low end of the range given.

observations.location: PDF p. 19 (printed p. 15)
observations.quote: the average review time for an EB-5 filing can range from 5.5 hours for an I-829 removal of conditions petition to 40 hours for an I-924 application for a new regional center.
observations.notes: Average review time for a new regional center application according to USCIS documentation cited by GAO; high end of the range given.

observations.location: press release, 2nd paragraph
observations.quote: fraudulently sold more than $145 million in securities and collected $11 million in administrative fees from more than 250 investors primarily from China
observations.notes: SEC allegation when the case was unsealed: EB-5 money raised (securities sold) by A Chicago Convention Center and Intercontinental Regional Center Trust of Chicago; "more than" (lower bound). The 4th paragraph says the court froze "the remaining $145 million in investor assets". Headline says "$150 Million".

observations.location: press release, 2nd paragraph
observations.quote: fraudulently sold more than $145 million in securities and collected $11 million in administrative fees from more than 250 investors primarily from China
observations.notes: Investors in one regional-center offering ("more than 250", mainly from China), as alleged by the SEC; a count for one project, not an average.

observations.location: press release, 2nd and 6th paragraphs
observations.quote: fraudulently sold more than $145 million in securities and collected $11 million in administrative fees from more than 250 investors primarily from China
observations.notes: Administrative fees collected from EB-5 investors on top of the investment (6th paragraph: "More than $11 million in administrative fees were collected"); the SEC alleges more than 90 percent had been spent.

observations.location: press release, 6th paragraph
observations.quote: convince investors to wire a minimum of $500,000 apiece plus a $41,500 "administrative fee" to U.S. bank accounts
observations.notes: Administrative fee per investor in this offering, on top of the USD 500,000 investment, as alleged by the SEC.

observations.location: press release, 3rd paragraph
observations.quote: More than $2.5 million of these funds were directed to Sethi's personal bank account in Hong Kong.
observations.notes: Part of the administrative fees, as alleged by the SEC ("more than"); not a court finding.

observations.location: investor alert, 5th paragraph
observations.quote: In another case, SEC v. A Chicago Convention Center, et al. , the SEC and USCIS coordinated to halt an alleged $156 million investment fraud.
observations.notes: Size of the alleged fraud as given in the October 2013 alert (the February 2013 press release said more than USD 145 million in securities sold plus USD 11 million in fees). Allegation, not a finding.

observations.location: press release, 4th paragraph
observations.quote: raising more than $350 million from investors to construct ski resort facilities and a biomedical research facility in Vermont
observations.notes: EB-5 money raised for the Jay Peak / Vermont projects, as alleged by the SEC ("more than", lower bound); previously only in the notes of the existing rows.

observations.quote: Visas shall be made available, in a number not to exceed 10,000, to qualified immigrants seeking to enter the United States for the purpose of engaging in a new commercial enterprise
observations.notes: Annual ceiling set by the Immigration Act of 1990 for EB-5 (employment creation) visas, in force from 1 October 1991 / FY1992 (sec. 161). Spouses and children count against it.

observations.quote: Not less than 3,000 of the visas made available under this paragraph in each fiscal year shall be reserved for qualified immigrants who establish a new commercial enterprise
observations.notes: Minimum annual reservation for investors creating employment in a targeted employment area (rural or at least 150 percent of the national unemployment rate). "Not less than".

observations.quote: shall set aside 300 visas annually for five years to include such aliens as are eligible for admission under section 203(bX5)
observations.notes: Regional Center pilot program: 300 EB-5 visas a year (including spouses and children) for five years, starting between 1 October 1992 and 1 October 1993. Text as OCR-ed in the govinfo PDF ("203(bX5)" = 203(b)(5)).

observations.quote: ‘‘(aa) 20 percent shall be reserved for qualified immigrants who invest in a rural area;
observations.notes: Share of the EB-5 visas available each fiscal year reserved for this set-aside, in force on enactment (15 Mar 2022). Unused reserved visas carry over in the same category for one year, then become generally available.

observations.quote: ‘‘(bb) 10 percent shall be reserved for qualified immigrants who invest in an area designated by the Secretary of Homeland Security under clause (ii) as a high unemployment area; and
observations.notes: Share of the EB-5 visas available each fiscal year reserved for this set-aside, in force on enactment (15 Mar 2022). Unused reserved visas carry over in the same category for one year, then become generally available.

observations.quote: ‘‘(cc) 2 percent shall be reserved for qualified immigrants who invest in infrastructure projects.
observations.notes: Share of the EB-5 visas available each fiscal year reserved for this set-aside, in force on enactment (15 Mar 2022). Unused reserved visas carry over in the same category for one year, then become generally available.

events.title: EB-5 investor visa category takes effect (FY1992)
events.description: Under sec. 161 of the Immigration Act of 1990, the new preference system, including the employment-creation (EB-5) category created by sec. 121, took effect on 1 October 1991 and applied from fiscal year 1992.
events.quote: the amendments made by this title shall take effect on October 1, 1991, and apply beginning with fiscal year 1992.

events.title: USCIS sets up an EB-5 fraud specialist unit in FDNS
events.description: In November 2013 USCIS established a fraud specialist unit for the EB-5 Program within its Fraud Detection and National Security directorate, after moving EB-5 work from the California Service Center to the new Immigrant Investor Program Office in Washington.
events.quote: In November 2013, USCIS also established a fraud specialist unit for the EB-5 Program within FDNS.

events.title: SEC sues Luca International over Ponzi-like scheme targeting EB-5 investors
events.description: The SEC filed a civil enforcement action (SEC v. Luca Int'l Group, N.D. Cal.) alleging a Ponzi-like scheme and affinity fraud targeting, among others, Chinese citizens seeking permanent residence through EB-5.
events.quote: In July 2015, SEC initiated another EB-5-related civil enforcement action alleging that defendants ran a Ponzi-like scheme and affinity fraud

new_indicators.name: Petitions to remove residence conditions decided
new_indicators.definition: Petitions to remove the conditions on an investor's conditional permanent residence (e.g. US Form I-829) completed in a period (approved plus denied, plus other closures where the source counts them), regardless of when filed.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa4 for the "Total Completions" column of the USCIS all-forms reports.

new_indicators.name: Applications to designate an investment-pooling entity decided
new_indicators.definition: Applications for designation or amendment of an intermediary entity that pools investor money (e.g. US EB-5 regional center, Forms I-924 / I-956) completed by the programme authority in a period (approvals plus denials, including terminations where the source counts them).

new_indicators.name: Applications to designate an investment-pooling entity pending
new_indicators.definition: Applications for designation or amendment of an intermediary entity that pools investor money (e.g. US EB-5 regional center, Forms I-924 / I-956) awaiting a decision at a date. A stock.

new_indicators.name: Programme filings approved (other forms)
new_indicators.definition: Filings under a programme's forms other than the main investor petition, the petition to remove conditions and intermediary designation applications (e.g. EB-5 project applications I-956F, annual statements I-924A/I-956G, bona fides I-956H, promoter registrations I-956K) approved in a period. Use breakdown form=.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa4; companion of programme_filings_received.

new_indicators.name: Programme filings denied (other forms)
new_indicators.definition: Filings under a programme's other forms (as for programme_filings_approved) denied in a period. Use breakdown form=.

new_indicators.name: Programme filings decided (other forms)
new_indicators.definition: Filings under a programme's other forms (as for programme_filings_approved) completed in a period (approvals plus denials, plus other closures where the source counts them). Use breakdown form=.

new_indicators.name: Programme filings pending (other forms)
new_indicators.definition: Filings under a programme's other forms (as for programme_filings_approved) awaiting a decision at a date. A stock. Use breakdown form=.

new_indicators.name: Fraud tips and complaints about a programme received
new_indicators.definition: Tips, complaints and referrals received by an authority (e.g. a securities regulator) about possible fraud connected with an investment-migration programme, in a period.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa4 (GAO-15-696: over 100 SEC tips Jan 2013-Jan 2015).

new_indicators.name: Fees collected from programme investors by an intermediary (total)
new_indicators.definition: Total fees (administrative, placement or similar) that a private intermediary or project collected from programme investors on top of the qualifying investment, in a case or period, as stated by an authority. Per-investor amounts go in rbi_intermediary_fee_per_investor.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa4 (SEC 2013-20: USD 11 million of administrative fees in the Chicago Convention Center case).

ledger.contains: GAO report (Aug 2015, 58 pp.) on EB-5 fraud risks and economic-benefit reporting: background on the programme and forms, USCIS/interagency fraud risk assessments, FDNS staffing and training, SEC tips and enforcement actions, open investigations, information-system limits, site visits, I-829 interviews, staffing of the Immigrant Investor Program Office, use of economic models (RIMS II), USCIS method for counting jobs and investment, one regional center project case study, the I-526/I-829 completion cohort, the Commerce (ESA) study, recommendations and DHS comments (image pages OCR-ed: no numbers). Extracted (with the 5 rows and 1 event already in the data): 73,730 jobs FY1990-FY2014 (USCIS minimum method); EB-5 visas issued FY2011 (almost 3,000) and FY2014 (over 9,000); 95% of FY2014 investments in regional centers; over 100 SEC tips Jan 2013-Jan 2015; 35 securities-fraud investigations of the 59; FDNS authorized 21 / onboard 12 (May 2015); IPO 58 adjudicators and 22 economists (June 2015), 9 adjudicators before 2014; 95% using economic models and 90% of those RIMS II; ~90% TEA / 10% full amount; 32 investors at USD 1 million in FY2013; ~10,000 approved I-526 (inception-FY2011), ~7,400 approved I-829 (to FY2014), 26% without approved I-829; one project: 450 investors, USD 225 million (30% of ~USD 750 million), 10,500 jobs; events: FDNS EB-5 fraud unit (Nov 2013), SEC v. Luca (6 Jul 2015). Not recorded (not programme quantities, derived, or rules): statutory ~10,000 visas and 7.1%, USD 1m/500k amounts (in program_terms), 150% unemployment and 20,000 population definitions; ~900 applications suspended in 1998 (GAO-05-256 history); a targeted sample of ~150 high-risk petitions; GAO sample sizes (28 files, 16 adjudicators, 8 economists, survey answers); 8 additional FDNS hires, 8 of 12 staff trained, six EB-5 University sessions; ELIS delay and USD 1 billion cost; IPO analysis that ~160 industries cannot create 10 jobs per USD 500,000, pharma 5 vs construction 10-12 jobs; GAO calculations (23 jobs per investor, 4,500 vs 6,000 jobs, USD 16 million difference, 315 investors / 3,150 jobs pro-rata counterfactual, ~2,600 remainder in notes); 316 million US population.

GAO report (Sept 2016, 32 pp.) on USCIS fraud detection in EB-5: background, risk assessments (source-of-funds study, random site-visit pilot, national-security review), forms, interviews, FinCEN checks, FDNS resources, compliance unit, proposed fee increases, paper-file problem and digitisation study, Fraud Risk Framework comparison, hypothetical fraud risk profile (Appendix I), DHS comments (image pages OCR-ed: no numbers). Extracted (with the 2 rows already in the data: 851 regional centers, 61 terminated, Aug 2016): FDNS authorized positions 25 FTE; 50 planned pilot site visits (four states, from Aug 2016); ~14,000 petitions and applications expected a year; average review time 5.5 hours (I-829) to 40 hours (I-924); fees then in force (I-526 USD 1,500; I-924 USD 6,230) as program_terms. Not recorded: proposed fees (I-526 USD 3,675, I-924 USD 17,795, new I-924A USD 3,035; proposals, in force from Dec 2016 per other sources); ~1,000 pages per filing and 14 million pages a year; GAO samples (10 I-829 denials FY2010-2014, 10 regional centers, 20 files); statutory amounts and definitions; Fraud Risk Framework example table (hypothetical).

Immigration Act of 1990 (111 pp.). EB-5 content read in full: sec. 121(a) INA 203(b)(5) employment creation (10,000 visas, 3,000 reserved for targeted employment areas, USD 1,000,000 capital, TEA amount not below half, high-employment amount up to 3 times, 10 jobs, TEA and rural-area definitions), sec. 121(b) INA 216A conditional residence (two years, 90-day filing window, interview within 90 days, termination), USD-free criminal penalty (up to 5 years for entrepreneurship fraud), deportation ground (p. 101), effective date 1 Oct 1991 / FY1992 (sec. 161, p. 31). Extracted: visa ceiling 10,000 and TEA reservation 3,000 (visa_places_planned); event for 1 Oct 1991 entry into force. Already in the data: launch event, USD 1,000,000 term, programme record. Rules without a fitting table (kept here): one-half/three-times capital adjustment powers, 10-job requirement, 2-year conditional period, 90-day windows, 5-year penalty. Out of scope: the rest of the Act (family and other employment preferences, worldwide levels 140,000 etc., diversity visas, naturalisation, nonimmigrant, enforcement provisions).

FY1993 Commerce-Justice-State appropriations act (48 pp.). Only sec. 610 (PDF p. 47) concerns EB-5: Regional Center pilot program, 300 visas set aside annually for five years (from 1 Oct 1992, no later than 1 Oct 1993), indirect job counting by reasonable methodologies. Extracted: 300 visas a year (visa_places_planned, route=regional_center); the creation event is already in the data. Out of scope: all other appropriations (INS budget lines, other agencies).

Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022 (1,068 pp.). Division BB, EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (PDF pp. 1022-1061), read in full: sec. 102 reserved visas (20% rural, 10% high unemployment, 2% infrastructure, carry-over), DHS-only high-unemployment designation (150%, 2-year designations), USD 1,050,000 / 800,000 and automatic CPI adjustment from 1 Jan 2027 (75% TEA ratio, round down to USD 50,000), definitions, child age-out, concurrent filing; sec. 103 Regional Center Program through 30 Sep 2027, indirect jobs up to 90% (75% construction), record keeping 5 years, audits every 5 years, I-956F business plans, site visits, redeployment, annual statements, sanctions (fines up to 10% of capital), bona fides, foreign-government ban, securities compliance, EB-5 Integrity Fund (USD 20,000 / 10,000 annual, USD 1,000 per petition, at least 1/3 for investigations abroad), promoters, source of funds (7 years of tax returns), good-faith investors (180 days), national interest and fraud denials, appeals, fund administration, OFAC checks; effective 60 days after enactment; sec. 104 conditional residence changes (site visit after 2 years, 1-year extension); sec. 105 filing order; sec. 106 fee study, processing goals and IT fee up to 1%; sec. 107 transparency; sec. 108 protection of petitions filed by 30 Sep 2026. Extracted: set-aside shares 20/10/2% (visa_places_planned_share) and the six statutory processing goals (processing_time_goal_days). Already in the data: investment terms USD 1,050,000 and 800,000, Integrity Fund fees, signing event and 30 Sep 2026 protection event; dates 14 May 2022, 15 Mar 2024, 1 Jan 2027 and 30 Sep 2027 are already events from other sources. Rules without a fitting table (kept here): 90/75% indirect-job limits, 10% fine cap, 1/3 fund use, 5-year audits/records, 180-day and other deadlines, USD 1,000,000 bona fides threshold, 7-year tax records. Out of scope: the rest of the Act (all other appropriations and divisions, incl. USCIS operating funds for E-Verify on PDF pp. 284-286).

Joint SEC/USCIS investor alert (1 Oct 2013) on EB-5 investment scams: how the programme works, two cases (SEC v. Ramirez / USA Now regional center promising a 5% return; SEC v. A Chicago Convention Center, an alleged USD 156 million fraud with more than 90 percent of administrative fees spent), due-diligence steps and warning signs. Extracted: USD 156 million alleged fraud size (rbi_investment_total, claim); the event is already in the data. Not recorded: the promised 5% return and the "more than 90 percent" of fees spent (in notes of the Chicago rows); the rest is guidance without numbers.

SEC press release 2013-20 (8 Feb 2013): charges and asset freeze against Anshoo Sethi, A Chicago Convention Center and Intercontinental Regional Center Trust of Chicago. Extracted: more than USD 145 million in securities sold, more than 250 investors, USD 11 million in administrative fees, USD 41,500 fee per investor, more than USD 2.5 million to a personal account (all SEC allegations, status claim); the event is already in the data. Not recorded: headline "$150 Million" (rounded), "more than 90 percent" of fees spent and the frozen "remaining $145 million" (notes), USD 1 million / 500,000 programme amounts and 10 jobs (rules already in program_terms), 29-year-old, 15 and 35 years of claimed experience (personal/company details).

SEC press release 2016-69 (14 Apr 2016): fraud charges, asset freeze and receivership in the Jay Peak / Vermont EB-5 case. Extracted: more than USD 350 million raised from investors (rbi_investment_total, claim); already in the data: more than USD 200 million misused and USD 50 million on personal expenses, and the event. Not recorded: the number of defendants (seven limited partnerships, four relief defendants), which are case parties rather than programme counts.

USCIS quarterly all-forms report FY2020 (2 pp.): received, approved, denied and pending by quarter (Q1-Q4) and fiscal-year-to-date received and approved, for every USCIS form. EB-5 rows: I-526, I-829, I-924, I-924A. Rows for every EB-5 form (I-526 incl. legacy/standalone/I-526E editions, I-829, I-924, I-924A, I-956, I-956F, I-956G, I-956H, I-956K, as present) and every printed cell: quarter received, approved, denied, total completions, pending (as of quarter end), median processing time (months), and fiscal-year-to-date received, approved, denied, total completions. Not recorded as numbers: cells shown "D" (disclosure standards not met) or "H" (masked so D cannot be deduced) and "N/A"; processing-time cells shown "-" where a form had no completions (I-924/I-956G/I-956H etc.), which are not zero-month times. Zeros printed "-" are recorded as 0 with a note. Out of scope: all non-EB-5 forms (family, employment, humanitarian, naturalisation etc.) and the all-forms totals. Quarter sums checked against the FY columns (I-526, I-829 received and approved; I-924 approved; all add up).
